transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel constantly on edge at the plant and even around loud machines anywhere, like I can’t ever relax or let my guard down. It has gotten so exhausting, and my supervisor and a close friend finally urged me to come in and get some help.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'on edge' - are you experiencing any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you're around loud machines or at the plant?

Yes, I definitely do. When I'm at the plant or around loud noises, my chest gets incredibly tight, my hands sweat, and I flinch at any sudden sound. My shoulders are always tense and shrugged up to my ears, like I'm constantly bracing for some disaster.

Have you experienced any recurring, distressing memories or flashbacks related to a specific traumatic event, or do your symptoms seem more related to a general state of anxiety or fear in certain situations?

It's definitely tied to a specific event—out of nowhere, I will suddenly see my coworker crushed in that machine as clearly as if it's happening right in front of me again. My chest tightens, my hands sweat, and I feel like I'm right back on that factory floor hearing him scream and the alarms blaring. It's not just general anxiety; it's like I'm reliving that horrible day all over again.
Can you estimate how long after the traumatic event at the plant these flashbacks and physical symptoms started, and have they been constant since then or have they changed over time?

These flashbacks and physical reactions started happening right after the accident a little over two years ago. They have been ongoing ever since, but they became much worse and more entrenched recently when the company installed the new press line in that same area.
Have you been avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of the traumatic event, and if so, how has this avoidance affected your daily life and relationships?

Yes, I actively avoid the new press line at work, and I've completely quit my book club, church groups, and community theater because triggers like power tools or machine oil make me feel like I'm going to fall apart. It has severely impacted my life—I've cut my hours, turned down promotions, and isolated myself from friends because I'm just too exhausted and on edge to show up.
Do you often have difficulty falling or staying asleep, or experience difficulty concentrating, as part of your overall state of being 'on edge'?

Yes, my sleep is a total mess. I lie awake for hours replaying the day, and even when I do drift off, I jerk awake at any little creak or passing truck. I'm usually wide awake by three or four in the morning, which leaves me completely wrung out and exhausted at work.
Do you find yourself constantly scanning your surroundings for potential dangers or threats, even when you're not at the plant or around loud machines?

Yes, I absolutely do, even when I'm at church or just in the grocery store. I find myself constantly scanning for exits, flinching at any loud bang or clank, and keeping my shoulders tensed up to my ears like I'm bracing for another disaster.
Can you describe how your constant scanning for potential dangers affects your relationships with family and friends, and do you feel like you're able to turn it off or relax around them?

No, I can't turn it off or relax at all, even around the people I care about. I'm constantly scanning for exits and flinching at loud noises whether I'm at church or just in the grocery store. Because I'm so exhausted and on edge, I've stopped going to church groups, book club, and theater, which has completely isolated me from my friends.
